title: Fuengirola Pool League rules (EPA 8-ball) — quick reference
note: Short summaries written for quick use at the table. If a summary and the official rules ever disagree, the official rules and the referee win.

rules.tags: referee final decision sportsmanlike spirit unsporting
rules.text: 8 Ball Pool, played in a sportsmanlike way. The referee is the sole judge of fair and unfair play and can take whatever action is needed to enforce the rules. The referee's decision is final.

rules.tags: balls groups colours colors stripes solids reds yellows table pockets
rules.text: Six-pocket rectangular table with 15 object balls plus the cue ball. There are two groups of object balls and the black 8. Sets are either numbered (solids 1–7, stripes 9–15) or plain colours (reds and yellows).

rules.tags: win object black 8 eight group pot
rules.text: Pot all of your group in any order, then legally pot the black 8 to win the frame.

rules.tags: rack spot triangle
rules.text: Rack the balls with the black 8 on the 8-ball spot, where the lines between the centre and corner pockets cross.

rules.tags: coin toss flip order who breaks
rules.text: A coin flip decides order of play. The winner either breaks or makes the opponent break.

rules.tags: break foul break rack two visits cushion baulk line illegal
rules.text: The breaker plays from anywhere on or behind the baulk line at the triangle. They must pot at least one object ball or drive at least two object balls to a cushion. If they don't, it's a foul break: the balls are re-racked and the opponent starts with 2 visits.

rules.tags: 8 ball black eight potted on the break re-rack
rules.text: If the black 8 is potted on the break, re-rack and the same player breaks again. There is no penalty, even if other balls or the cue ball were also potted or left the table.

rules.tags: group nominate choose stripes solids first pot both groups
rules.text: The first object ball a player legally pots (including after a foul) sets their group. If balls from both groups are potted on that shot, the player must nominate a group before play continues.

rules.tags: open table groups undecided nothing potted break
rules.text: If no object ball is potted from a legal break, players take turns playing at either group until someone makes a legal pot, which decides the groups.

rules.tags: foul before groups decided open table any ball first shot
rules.text: If a foul happens (other than the 8 on the break) and balls are potted before groups have been decided, those balls are ignored when deciding groups. The incoming player may play any ball, including the 8, on the first shot, and the first legal pot then decides the groups.

rules.tags: continue another shot turn visit keep going
rules.text: A legal pot earns another shot. A player keeps shooting until they fail to pot one of their own balls or commit a foul.

rules.tags: combination shot first ball hit
rules.text: Combination shots are allowed as long as the first ball hit is one of your own group, or any ball on the first shot after a foul (see 6(c)).

rules.tags: in off scratch cue ball potted pocket
rules.text: In off: the cue ball is potted.

rules.tags: hit opponent ball first wrong ball
rules.text: Hitting an opponent's ball first with the cue ball, except on the first shot after a foul.

rules.tags: miss fail to hit no contact air shot
rules.text: Failing to hit any ball with the cue ball.

rules.tags: jump shot jump over ball
rules.text: Jump shot: the cue ball jumps over any part of a ball before it contacts a ball.

rules.tags: hit black 8 first early eight
rules.text: Hitting the 8 first before all of your own balls are potted, except on the first shot after a foul.

rules.tags: pot opponent ball opponents balls potted
rules.text: Potting any of the opponent's balls, except on the first shot after a foul.

rules.tags: ball off the table jumped off object ball respot spot
rules.text: An object ball or the 8 that goes off the table is returned to the 8-ball spot, or as near as possible to it without touching another ball, on the line between that spot and the centre of the baulk line.

rules.tags: cue ball off the table jumped off in hand
rules.text: If the cue ball goes off the table, it is played from hand (see 8(b)). A ball counts as off the table if it comes to rest anywhere other than on the bed of the table.

rules.tags: touch ball clothing sleeve body moved ball
rules.text: Clothing or body touching any ball. The one exception is the cue ball after the referee has called a foul and the player is entitled to cue ball in hand (see 6(b)).

rules.tags: foot floor feet off the ground sitting
rules.text: Not having at least one foot on the floor.

rules.tags: touch other ball with cue
rules.text: Playing or touching with the cue any ball other than the cue ball.

rules.tags: ferrule shaft side of cue not tip
rules.text: Striking the cue ball with any part of the cue other than the tip.

rules.tags: out of turn wrong player
rules.text: Playing out of turn.

rules.tags: moving balls not at rest too early
rules.text: Playing before the balls have come to rest.

rules.tags: respot before replaced
rules.text: Playing before balls that need re-spotting have been re-spotted.

rules.tags: double hit twice
rules.text: Striking the cue ball with the cue more than once.

rules.tags: push stroke tip contact
rules.text: Push stroke: the tip is still touching the cue ball when it makes contact with the object ball, or the tip stays obviously in contact once the cue ball has started moving forward.

rules.tags: nominate group both groups potted forgot
rules.text: Failing to nominate a group when balls of both groups are potted with the first legal pot.

rules.tags: foul break cushions two balls
rules.text: Foul break: failing to pot an object ball or drive at least two object balls to a cushion.

rules.tags: penalty lose visit two visits
rules.text: After any foul, the player who fouled loses their next visit to the table, so their opponent gets two visits.

rules.tags: cue ball in hand two visits baulk line where it lies ask referee
rules.text: With two visits, the player can play the cue ball from where it lies if it is on the table, or play it from any position on or behind the baulk line. Moving the cue ball this way does not count as a shot or a visit. Ask the referee to hand you the cue ball.

rules.tags: first shot after foul any ball without penalty second visit
rules.text: On the first shot of the first visit only, the incoming player may play the cue ball onto any ball without penalty, including an opponent's ball or the 8. If they don't pot a ball during that first visit, play moves on to their second visit, which starts when the cue ball is struck for the first shot of that visit.

rules.tags: lose game early 8 black potted too soon
rules.text: Potting the 8 before all the balls of your own group are down loses the frame, except on the break (see 4(d)).

rules.tags: foul while potting 8 black lose
rules.text: Committing any foul while potting the 8 loses the frame, except on the break (see 4(d)).

rules.tags: pot 8 and another ball same shot lose exception after foul only 8 left
rules.text: Potting the 8 and any other ball on the same shot loses the frame. The exception is after a foul when only the 8 and ball(s) of the opponent's group are left on the table: then, with the first shot of the first visit, the player may legally pot the 8 along with ball(s) by any combination and in any order.

rules.tags: no attempt to play own ball deliberately lose
rules.text: A player who clearly makes no attempt to play a ball of their own group loses the frame.

rules.tags: cue ball touching object ball frozen play away
rules.text: If the cue ball is touching an object ball, you must play away from it. Moving that object ball is a foul.

rules.tags: cue ball touching ball legal to play deemed played frozen
rules.text: If the cue ball is touching any ball you are legally allowed to play, you are deemed to have played that ball. If the cue ball then fails to contact any ball, or strikes an opponent's ball or the 8, the shot is fair and not a foul.

rules.tags: cue ball in hand baulk line place
rules.text: Cue ball in hand: it is played from any position on or behind the baulk line, in any direction.

rules.tags: player in control table touch ball falls in pocket after foul
rules.text: A player is in control of the table from the moment their body, cue or clothing touches the table before their shot, through their whole visit, until the opponent does the same before theirs. Any ball (including the 8) that drops into a pocket in that time counts as potted, and the player in control takes the penalty or benefit. Once the cue ball has been struck, a legal shot must be completed, and a ball falling in does NOT cancel out a foul.

rules.tags: frame over game complete 8 black potted rest
rules.text: The frame is complete when the 8 is potted in any pocket and all the remaining balls have come to rest, except on the break (see 4(d)).

rules.tags: stalemate no legal shot restart re-rack stuck safety battle
rules.text: If a legal shot cannot be played, by accident or design, the frame is restarted by the player who started that frame. The referee should not allow many visits where neither player tries the opening pot that decides the groups (unless progress is being made). If that player started the frame because the opponent fouled the break, they break again on the restart, not the opponent who fouled.

rules.tags: definition shot
rules.text: A 'shot' means striking the ball once.

rules.tags: definition visit turn
rules.text: A 'visit' is one turn at the table, made up of one shot or a series of shots.

rules.tags: definition break
rules.text: The 'break' is the first shot of a frame, or the first shot of a frame being restarted.

rules.tags: coaching advice help unsporting
rules.text: Coaching counts as unsportsmanlike behaviour (see rule 1).

rules.tags: referee advise rules asked
rules.text: A referee may advise on the rules, but only if asked.

rules.tags: nominate group breaker obligation
rules.text: Both players are obliged to make sure the breaking player nominates a group of object balls.

rules.tags: slow play time excessive
rules.text: The referee should make sure nobody takes excessive time over a shot, acting in line with the competition rules or guidance.

rules.tags: doubles talking partner conversation coaching
rules.text: In doubles, once a player is in control of the table, conversation with anyone else, including their partner, is unsporting.
